name: "Extreme War Machine" Corey Irons

tenures.note: Won the vacant Hardcore Championship on the promotion's first card since its hiatus (2 May 2001); lost it to Johnny Eastland; won the vacant Television Championship from the Iron Predator (9 May 2001); beat Eastland in the tournament final to become the first MECW World Champion (26 May 2001).

tenures.source: its own House Blend house-show reports posted 29 July and 18 August 2002

Won a four-corners match on the promotion's own 1 September 2002 broadcast; also fought to a double disqualification with Catastrophe and Jeff Keenan on the 16 August 2002 pay-per-view alongside partner Ajax Carter.

tenures.note: Appeared in a vignette on 25 May 2005 recounting a career cut short by years of overwork and injury, naming Verhoeven, Vitrone, and Eddie Jacobs among the opponents who left him scarred, and describing forfeited matches and unfinished business; did not wrestle. Delivered a rooftop monologue about returning from career-ending injuries on 8 June 2005, met a returning Sonya Benedict in the parking lot beforehand with valet Exotica at his side, then won his own first sanctioned UWF match against "Gunman" Danny Cole by submission (the Web of Death sharpshooter). Submitted "Atomic Son" Sean Malcomb with the Web of Death in a Road to the Gold qualifier on 22 June 2005, advancing toward the battle royal. Agreed backstage on 23 July 2005 to watch over Sonya Benedict against the Hands of Death at Chad Grimsson's own request, extracting a promise of reciprocal help against Trey DaMann. Overcame a pre-match backstage beatdown from Trey DaMann to team with the Sons of Cacaphony and pin Caliban for the win on 3 August 2005. Teamed with Sonya Benedict in the Cupid's Revenge Blind Date Tournament on 14 February 2006, pinned by a tandem shining wizard from Sabbath and Moira Faith after asking his own partner to focus on winning rather than her feud with Angel; shared a dockside scene beforehand recalling his late wife, Ashley, killed in a plane crash five years earlier. Beat "Violent" Victor Frost by pinfall (the Lariat) on 7 June 2006, reversing a dragon sleeper into a standing powerslam beforehand; delivered a promo before the match reflecting on a year of complacency since his own Gold Rush appearance. Sought out new outside consultant "The Doomsayer" Kyle Lee on 28 April 2007 for advice on breaking out of a career rut, gifting him a bottle of Jack Daniels; discussed the visit afterward with girlfriend "Twilight Angel" Sonya Benedict, who had a title belt of her own to show him. Did not wrestle.

caption: Won MECW's Hardcore, Television and inaugural World Championships across spring 2001, becoming the promotion's first World Champion at its debut pay-per-view, Hell Night.

name: "The Exterminator" Johnny Eastland

tenures.note: Defeated Corey Irons for the Hardcore Championship; later defeated Jaguar for the vacant Television Championship; lost the World Championship tournament final to Corey Irons.

caption: Took the Hardcore Championship from Corey Irons and later added the vacant Television Championship, but lost the tournament final for the first MECW World Championship.

identity.note: Shares the nickname "The Exterminator" with a wrestler already recorded on another wing under that bare ring name. Different full name (Johnny Eastland) and no shared operator, roster or chronology evidence; recorded distinct under the standing no-merge default.

name: Iron Predator

tenures.note: MECW's first Hall of Fame inductee (3 April 2001); lost the vacant Television Championship to Corey Irons on 9 May 2001. The promotion's own words separately call him a "former MECW World Champion," though no World Championship reign for him survives in the held record (the title first attested is Corey Irons's win of 26 May 2001).

caption: MECW's first Hall of Fame inductee, later beaten by Corey Irons for the vacant Television Championship.

name: Doyle

tenures.note: Named among four wrestlers drawing a first-round bye into the World Championship tournament ahead of Hell Night (26 May 2001); no further appearance survives.

caption: Drew a first-round bye into MECW's inaugural World Championship tournament; no match result for him survives.

name: Jaguar

tenures.note: Billed as a "rising star"; lost the vacant Television Championship to Johnny Eastland.

caption: Billed as a rising star against Johnny Eastland for the vacant Television Championship, which he lost.

identity.note: Shares the exact name Jaguar with wrestlers already recorded on two other wings. No shared operator, roster or chronology evidence links this MECW billing to either; recorded distinct under the standing no-merge default for a recurring name.
